stops.note: 'staff, spoke of a wheel, ray of light'; centuries later the same word gave English 'radiation' and 'radio'
short for radiotelegraphy; Guglielmo Marconi received the first transatlantic radio signal at St John's, Newfoundland, in December 1901
a palindrome acronym for RAdio Detection And Ranging, coined in 1940 by US Navy officers Samuel Tucker and F. R. Furth; Britain, which called it RDF, adopted 'radar' in 1943

current_meaning: a system that detects distant objects using reflected radio waves
